name: Episcopal Church (United States)

citations.excerpt: After the American Revolution, the Episcopal Church was formed in 1789 and secured a succession of bishops and approved a Book of Common Prayer.

facts.value_before_verify: 1789, after the American Revolution. Colonial roots from the early 17th century

citations.excerpt: was supported by the Church of England through the Society for the Propagation of the Gospel, and technically under the jurisdiction of the Bishop of London.

facts.value: An Anglican church based in the United States, in full communion with the other churches of the Anglican Communion. It is a federal union of dioceses and accepts the Apostles' and Nicene Creeds. It also has dioceses outside the United States.

citations.excerpt: The Episcopal Church's form of government is a federal union, consisting of 111 dioceses
The church accepts two creeds: the Apostles' and the Nicene.
Full communion has been established among other churches of the Anglican Communion
Dioceses outside the United States are: Haiti, Virgin Islands, Puerto Rico

facts.value_before_verify: The Anglican church of the United States, a federal union of dioceses that accepts the Apostles' and Nicene Creeds. It also has dioceses outside the United States.
